note: The screens a compatibility session promises to render like the oracle, and the terms on which a capture pair may be compared. The presentation promise in profile.json names clonk-org/clonk-rs#587 as pending evidence, and this file is the detail behind it. Screens whose artwork or branding is port-authored are compared on the `layout` term rather than pixel equality - see `comparison_terms` and `port_assets`, decided in clonk-org/clonk-rs#1298.

pointer.note: Route this no-button logical position through each engine's production input path immediately before every capture render. The inset keeps the native 50-pixel CursorLarge glyph fully visible and makes ambient host pointer position irrelevant without suppressing product output.

capture.note: One resolution, scale, and pointer input for every screen: a comparison across different geometry or ambient mouse state proves nothing, and 1280x720 at scale 100 is what docs/RENDERING_PARITY.md's live C++ captures already use.

tolerance.note: The software renderer is the exact oracle, so a CPU capture may not differ at all. GPU composition carries the one-byte cross-driver tolerance docs/RENDERING_PARITY.md already documents for readback.

screens.description: Scenario selection subtree, including the folder listing and the selected-scenario panel.
Network start/lobby screen with its client and player lists.
Scenario loader screen with its progress bar and process log.
In-game upper board, message board and crew portraits.
Object-menu subtree, including the extra bar and tooltips.
Representative gameplay frame at a pinned scenario and frame number.

pixel.summary: Pixel equality within `tolerance`, over the whole frame minus any approved mask.
pixel.applies_to: Every screen whose pixels are all oracle-authored.

layout.summary: Widget geometry and text layout, not pixel equality: the same ordered controls, semantic roles, visibility, rects and resolved-line geometry. Captions and resolved line text are exact except at the individually declared port-asset nodes whose product text is intentionally different. The pixel term is not applied to a screen on this term, because the port's own artwork cannot equal the oracle's at any resolution - the difference is texture detail across the whole asset, not a rounding residue.
layout.applies_to: Screens that render one or more of `port_assets`.
layout.note: Chosen over shipping the oracle's branding and 1x art inside the profile. The port's identity and its super-resolved startup art are deliberate product features, and clonk-org/clonk-rs#587 forbids masking port-version text or product features, so no mask could make a pixel term pass on these screens either.

port_assets.summary: The port's own product identity: Logo.png, the version string and the footer line.
port_assets.authority: clonk-org/clonk-rs#587 (masks may not cover port-version text or product features)

port_assets.summary: Startup backgrounds replaced with 3x art in planet/Graphics.c4g (commit d239bbb9d): StartupScenSelBG.png, StartupPlrSelBG.png, StartupNetworkBG.png, StartupDlgPaper.png, StartupPlrPropBG.png, StartupScenSelIcons.png.
